question: A cylindrical rod has an outer curved surface area of 2200 cm² . If the length of the rod is 16 cm, then the outer radius (in cm) of the rod, correct to two places of decimal, is: (Take π = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Curved Surface Area of a cylinder = 2πrh

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 16 = 2200

⇒ r = (2200 × 7) ÷ (44 × 16)

⇒ r = 175 ÷ 8 = 21.875 cm

⇒ r ≈ 21.88 cm (rounded to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 21.88 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer curved surface area (CSA) = 2200 cm²

Length (height) of the rod (h) = 16 cm

Value of π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder = 2πrh

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 16 = 2200

⇒ 44/7 × r × 16 = 2200

⇒ r = (2200 × 7) ÷ (44 × 16)

⇒ r = (50 × 7) ÷ 16

⇒ r = 350 ÷ 16

⇒ r = 21.875 cm

Rounding to two places of decimal:

⇒ r ≈ 21.88 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21.88 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

The total surface area encompasses both the curved surface and the two circular flat ends (top and base). It is given by the formula: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cylinder

The total capacity enclosed within the cylinder geometry is calculated by multiplying the base area by its height: Volume = πr²h.

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

When dealing with a hollow cylindrical pipe or tube having an outer radius R and an inner radius r, the volume of material used is determined by: Volume = πh(R² − r²).
